content.title: About
content.content: Refried beans with meat is a classic Mexican dish consisting of cooked beans that are mashed and fried until creamy, then mixed with finely chopped meat (usually beef or pork). The dish has a rich, slightly smoky flavor and is used as a side, a main course, or a filling for tacos, burritos, and other dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The term “refried” comes from the Spanish “refritos,” meaning “fried again.”
Traditionally the beans are dried black or pinto beans that are soaked and boiled until soft before frying.
Original recipes use beef, but regional variations include pork, chicken, or even turkey.
It is often served with lime, cheese, sour cream, and fresh cilantro.
Refried beans became popular in the United States in the 1920s with the rise of Mexican restaurants.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Beans provide about 8 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are important for blood formation and nerve function.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Beans raise blood glucose slowly, which is beneficial for people prone to diabetes.

items.title: Meat adds B‑vitamins
items.content: B6 and B12 support energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared versions often contain added salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: If fatty meat is used, the dish can be high in saturated fats.

items.title: Anti‑nutrients
items.content: Raw beans contain phytates that reduce mineral absorption; proper soaking and cooking minimize them.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a side dish, taco or burrito filling, or as a main course with rice. Top with lime, fresh cilantro, shredded cheese, and sour cream for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked beans in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat thoroughly before eating to prevent bacterial growth.
